dish: Tacos with the house crisp-chewy fried shell and spicy salsa
n: Señor Taco, Plaza House (セニョール ターコ)
address: Plaza House 1F, 3-1-6 Kubota, Okinawa City, Okinawa 904-0023, Japan
w: Opened in 1984 inside Plaza House, Señor Taco is a pioneer of Okinawa's taco scene whose shells are fried crisp outside and chewy inside; it has been loved for more than 30 years and also serves Mexican dishes like enchiladas and onion rings.

n: Cafe Ocean, Gate 2 Street (カフェ オーシャン)
w: Founded in 1967, Ocean is the oldest taco shop on Koza's Gate 2 Street in front of Kadena Air Base, frying hand-made tortillas to order with a home-style sauce taught by Americans. A taco-and-music café-bar from the post-war 'A-sign' era.

dish: Aburi nankotsu soba (seared soft-bone sōki soba, a 'Koza Choice' city-certified brand dish)
n: Suba-dokoro Wachichi, Okinawa City (すば処 うゎちち)
w: An Okinawa-soba specialist in Hiyagon whose seared soft-bone soba was certified as an Okinawa City 'Koza Choice' brand; the clear pork-and-bonito broth comes with a choice of noodles from two well-known local noodle makers. It placed 12th in OTV Okitive's reader soba ranking TOP30.

dish: Hearty Okinawa soba (pork-bone & bonito broth), tonkatsu-soba set
n: Daruma Soba, Okinawa City (だるまそば)
w: A hearty, queue-drawing soba shop with a pork-bone and bonito broth, chewy noodles and an unusually long menu; listed 4th in KozaWeb's Okinawa City soba ranking and 19th in OTV Okitive's reader soba TOP30.

dish: House-made Okinawa soba noodles kneaded with ukon (turmeric), yomogi or beni-imo
w: A long-loved Yomitan soba house named after the old Kina banjo (district office), known for its house-made noodles, including turmeric-kneaded soba and yomogi or purple-sweet-potato variations.

dish: Ratatouille-sauce teriyaki chicken lunch set; Koza home-style plates inspired by 1970s base-era canned-food cooking
n: Player's Cafe, Koza (プレイヤーズカフェ)
address: 2-6-47 Chūō (Park Avenue), Okinawa City, Okinawa 904-0004, Japan
w: Opened in 1999 on Koza's Park Avenue, this café hosts live music of all genres and doubles as the lounge of Tripshot Hotels Koza; its menu draws on the owner's memories of 1970s Koza home cooking shaped by US-military canned goods. Ryukyu Shimpo reported its lunch sets as a hit with a wide range of customers.
